subtitle: Brick, Shadow and Escape in the Ahom Court of Rangpur

panels.shot: dramatic cutaway wide showing Rangpur palace above and its dark vaulted levels below
panels.action: Rajeswar Singha & the Chang-Rung Phukan stand in the torchlit depths of Talatal Ghar, while above them rises the sunlit mass of Kareng Ghar and the sprawling Rangpur palace complex.

dialogue.text: In the Ahom capital of Rangpur, Rajeswar Singha and his Chang-Rung Phukan shaped a palace with a secret: under the king’s throne, the earth itself learned to plan, store…and escape.

i18n.hi: अहोम राजधानी रंगपुर में, राजा राजेश्वर सिंघा और उनके चांग-रुंग फुकन ने ऐसा महल गढ़ा, जिसके सिंहासन के नीचे धरती ही सोचने, जमा करने…और निकल भागने लगी।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye wide of the Assam plains with rivers and a fortified capital emerging
panels.action: The braided channels of the Dikhow and neighbouring rivers wind through misty plains and groves as the fortified sprawl of Rangpur slowly emerges, moats and embankments holding the city above the floodplains.

dialogue.text: By the late seventeenth century, the Ahom kingdom held the Brahmaputra valley with earth embankments, stockades and courts that had learned from three centuries of flood, war and intrigue.

i18n.hi: सत्रहवीं सदी के अंत तक अहोम राज्य ने तीन सौ बरस की बाढ़, युद्ध और साज़िशों से सीखकर ब्रह्मपुत्र घाटी को मिट्टी बाँधों, किलों और न्याय दरबारों से थाम रखा था।

panels.shot: medium interior wide of an earlier king with architects over a ground plan
panels.action: In a timber hall lit by oil lamps, an earlier Ahom king, Rudra Singha, stands over floor plans while senior Chang-Rung Phukan officers unfurl palm-leaf drawings of a new brick palace for Rangpur.

dialogue.text: Rudra Singha and his successors dreamed of Rangpur as a new kind of capital—part court, part fortress—where brick and lime would give shape to Ahom power.

i18n.hi: रुद्र सिंघा और उनके वारिसों ने रंगपुर को नए किस्म की राजधानी सपना—आधा दरबार, आधा दुर्ग—जहाँ ईंट और चूना अहोम सत्ता को रूप दें।

panels.shot: low-angle construction wide with scaffolding around a rising palace
panels.action: Chang-Rung Phukan supervisors gesture from bamboo scaffolding as workers lay courses of brick with glistening rice-lime mortar, the lower masses of Talatal Ghar taking form beneath the rising Kareng Ghar.

dialogue.text: Under Sunenphaa and later Rajeswar Singha, the Chang-Rung Phukan turned that dream into courses of brick, arches of mortar and levels stacked above and below the ground.

i18n.hi: सुननफा और फिर राजेश्वर सिंघा के समय, चांग-रुंग फुकन ने उस सपने को ईंट की पंक्तियों, चूने के मेहराबों और ज़मीन के ऊपर–नीचे टिके मंज़िलों में बदल दिया।

panels.shot: close-up on hands mixing mortar and setting a vaulted brick arch
panels.action: Calloused hands press a paste of powdered lime, burnt brick and rice-husk into joints as an Ahom mason and a Chang-Rung Phukan officer carefully align bricks into the curve of a new vault.

dialogue.text: Their craft was patient. Burnt brick, slaked lime, pounded rice—materials turned to memory, binding each arch so the weight of a kingdom could rest upon it.

i18n.hi: उनकी कारीगरी धीरज से भरी थी। पक़ी ईंट, बुझा चूना, कूटा चावल—ये सब याद बनकर हर मेहराब को ऐसे बाँधते कि पूरे राज्य का बोझ उन पर टिक सके।

panels.shot: cutaway cross-section wide of Kareng Ghar above and Talatal Ghar below
panels.action: A cutaway view reveals the multi-storey Kareng Ghar with open halls above, while below lie Talatal Ghar’s dim vaulted chambers, staircases and corridors branching like roots through the soil.

dialogue.text: Kareng Ghar rose for ceremony and display. Talatal Ghar sank below it, a second palace in shadow, planned for stores, councils, armour, archives and the unspoken need to vanish.

i18n.hi: करेنگ घर रस्मों और शान के लिए उठा। उसके नीचे तलातल घर धँसा—साया-सा दूसरा महल, जहाँ गोदाम, सभाएँ, हथियार, अभिलेख और चुपचाप गुम हो जाने की ज़रूरत सोची गई।

panels.shot: medium interior of Rajeswar Singha descending into the underground with attendants
panels.action: Rajeswar Singha, robed yet unadorned, steps down a brick stair into the cool under-levels beside a leading Chang-Rung Phukan officer who holds a torch and a rolled palm-leaf plan.

dialogue.text: When Rajeswar Singha came to the throne in 1751, he inherited not only wars and offices, but this layered palace—half visible, half buried under his feet.

i18n.hi: १७५१ में राजेश्वर सिंघा गद्दी पर बैठे तो उन्हें सिर्फ़ युद्ध और ओहदे नहीं, ये तहदार महल भी मिला—आधा दिखता, आधा उनके पाँवों के नीचे दबा।

panels.shot: wide interior of a vaulted underground hall with rows of sealed jars and racks
panels.action: In a long, cool vaulted chamber, shelves of palm-leaf bundles and sealed grain jars line the walls as the Chang-Rung Phukan gestures, explaining the arrangement to the king in the wavering torchlight.

dialogue.text: “Mahārāj, this hall keeps grain, salt and records safe from fire, flood and siege.”

i18n.hi: “महाराज, ये दालान अनाज, नमक और रेकॉर्ड को आग, बाढ़ और घेराबंदी से बचाकर रखता है।”

panels.shot: close-up on racks of palm-leaf manuscripts and an architect marking them
panels.action: An officer of the Chang-Rung Phukan marks symbols on bundles of palm-leaf manuscripts stacked on wooden racks, while a small oil lamp throws sharp shadows over the neatly tied records.

dialogue.text: Here, the court’s mind was stored. Land grants, military rolls, orders of the Swargadeo—layered in script, guarded by brick, watched by the palace architects themselves.

i18n.hi: यहीं दरबार की सोच सँभालकर रखी थी। ज़मीन दान, फौजी रजिस्टर, स्वर्गदेव के हुक्म—काग़ज़ पर परत दर परत, ईंटों की हिफ़ाज़त में, और खुद महल के मिस्त्रियों की निगाह में।

panels.shot: medium of Rajeswar and the architect at a narrow, sloping corridor mouth
panels.action: Rajeswar Singha stands at the entrance of a narrow, sloping brick corridor that disappears into darkness, while the Chang-Rung Phukan bows slightly, indicating its unseen route with a careful hand.

dialogue.text: Tradition would later whisper of passages from these depths—towards the Dikhow’s bank, towards old Garhgaon—routes for a king who might one day need to outlive his own palace.

i18n.hi: बाद की परंपरा इन गहराइयों से निकलने वाली सुरंगों की फुसफुसाहट करेगी—कभी दिखाऊ के किनारे, कभी पुरानेगढ़गाँव की ओर—ऐसे रास्ते, जिनसे राजा एक दिन अपने ही महल से लंबा जी सके।

panels.shot: tight interior of the dark passage with a small inspection party
panels.action: By the light of a single torch, Rajeswar Singha, the Chang-Rung Phukan and two guards move cautiously along a low brick corridor, the ceiling arching just above their bowed heads.

dialogue.text: “We build only what we can guard, Maharāj. Beyond this, the earth keeps its own secrets.”

i18n.hi: “हम सिर्फ़ उतना ही बनाते हैं, महाराज, जितना खुद देख सकें। इसके आगे तो ज़मीन अपने राज़ खुद रखती है।”

panels.shot: exterior wide of Rangpur palace complex with defensive earthworks and rivers nearby
panels.action: A wide view shows the Talatal and Kareng Ghars within embanked earthworks and water channels, the distant glint of the Dikhow River hinting at the broader defensive landscape around Rangpur.

dialogue.text: Archaeology confirms only the nearest depths and walls, not a full sixteen-kilometre tunnel. The rest lives in chronicles and memory, where prudence and legend often share the same corridor.

i18n.hi: खुदाई से सिर्फ़ पास के तहख़ाने और दीवारें साबित हैं, पूरा सोलह किलोमीटर सुरंग नहीं। बाक़ी बात तो बख़्तनामा और यादों में रहती है, जहाँ एहतियात और अफ़साना एक ही गलियारा बाँट लेते हैं।

panels.shot: interior council wide in an underground hall with nobles and officers seated
panels.action: In a vaulted underground council hall, Rajeswar Singha sits on a raised platform as nobles and high officers, including the Chang-Rung Phukan, sit cross-legged, discussing maps and wooden counters.

dialogue.text: These were not mere hiding places. In Talatal Ghar’s cool halls, councils met, stores were tallied, routes of retreat weighed alongside ceremonies of rule above.

i18n.hi: ये सिर्फ़ छिपने की जगहें नहीं थीं। तलातल घर की ठंडी दालानों में सलाहें होतीं, गिनती होती, ऊपर राजकाज के साथ-साथ पीछे हटने की राहें भी तौली जातीं।

panels.shot: medium of the Chang-Rung Phukan supervising repairs after signs of damp
panels.action: The Chang-Rung Phukan inspects a damp patch on a vault ceiling as workers erect scaffolds and bring fresh mortar, while Rajeswar Singha watches, arms folded, in thoughtful silence.

dialogue.text: Rice-lime vaults needed care. In this office of builders, architecture was not a finished monument, but an ongoing duty, like policing or war.

i18n.hi: चावल-चूने के मेहराब देखभाल माँगते थे। इस मिस्त्री दफ़्तर में इमारत कोई पूरी हो चुकी निशानी नहीं, बल्कि पुलिस या युद्ध जैसी चलती हुई ज़िम्मेदारी थी।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide showing different kings and fashions over the same palace
panels.action: Over the unchanged mass of Talatal and Kareng Ghar, figures of Rudra Singha, Sunenphaa and Rajeswar Singha appear in succession, their attire and retinues shifting as years pass around the enduring brick.

dialogue.text: Rudra Singha conceived, Sunenphaa extended, Rajeswar Singha used and maintained. The underground palace was a long project of state, not the whim of one dramatic hour.

i18n.hi: रुद्र सिंघा ने सोचा, सुननफा ने बढ़ाया, राजेश्वर सिंघा ने चलाया और सँभाला। ये भूमिगत महल एक लम्बा राजकीय प्रोजेक्ट था, किसी एक नाटकीय पल की सनक नहीं।

panels.shot: modern-day wide of Talatal Ghar ruins with visitors walking through
panels.action: In the present day, weathered brick vaults and corridors of Talatal Ghar stand under an open sky, visitors treading carefully through the underground levels as sunlight falls in shafts from collapsed ceilings.

dialogue.text: Today the upper halls have lost their roofs; the underground survives in fragments. Yet every arch and passage still carries the weight of a court that once planned for absence as much as presence.

i18n.hi: आज ऊपर की हवेलियों की छतें उड़ चुकी हैं; नीचे का हिस्सा टुकड़ों में बचा है। फिर भी हर मेहराब और राह उस दरबार का वज़न लिए है, जो मौजूदगी जितनी ही ग़ैर-मौजूदगी की भी तैयारी करता था।

panels.shot: slow push-in close on Rajeswar Singha’s contemplative face half-lit in the underground
panels.action: In the dim light of a single torch, Rajeswar Singha’s face emerges from shadow, half-lit as he looks down a receding passage, the Chang-Rung Phukan’s figure a respectful silhouette beside him.

dialogue.text: In Rangpur’s underground palace, prudence became brick and corridor. It reminds us that lasting power is not only in grand entrances, but in the quiet, prepared paths by which a kingdom can endure and withdraw.

i18n.hi: रंगपुर के इस भूमिगत महल में दूरअंदेशी ईंट और गलियारे बन गई। ये याद दिलाता है कि टिकाऊ ताक़त सिर्फ़ धाँसू प्रवेश-द्वारों में नहीं, उन चुपचाप, तैयार राहों में भी होती है जिनसे कोई सल्तनत टिक भी सके और पीछे भी हट सके।

subtitle_i18n.en: Brick, Shadow and Escape in the Ahom Court of Rangpur
subtitle_i18n.hi: ईंट, साया और फ़रार — रंगपुर के अहोम दरबार में
